thread:
maria-ml: heads up — saw a reproducible cross-request token leak on the Llama-70b quant path. long-context + micro-batching seems to surface it. previous request prefixes are showing up in unrelated responses.

maria-ml: repro steps below (very small):
1) start streaming generate with prompt A (len ~ 12k tokens)
2) concurrent micro-batched request B (short) arrives and finishes
3) next generate for a new client returns tail tokens from A appended to B

maria-ml: attaching a short trace and a heap snapshot excerpt:
```
KV pages allocated: 128 
active frames: 94
free frames: 34
page-refs: [0, 1, 0, 2, ...]
observed: stale_page_id=57 reused_at_offset=4096 expected_zero
```

tim-infra: can you paste the exact command and whether this is dedicated or hosted? also is this on quantized kernels only?

maria-ml: hosted dev stack, dedicated repro on my dev machine too. command: `rlinfer serve --model llm-70b-qat --sequence_len 12288 --batch_shapes "[1x512, 4x128]"`
It's more common on QAT/4-bit paths but i saw one hit on fp16 when we had batching boundary misalignment.

asha-runtime: i ran the micro-batch profiler yesterday — when we switch kernel variants (small-batch kernel vs big-batch kernel) the kv stride/pack semantics differ slightly. if freelist reuse doesn't re-init the physical page, offsets can be off by one block because of different per-kernel padding.

asha-runtime: plausible root cause: allocator returns a page that was used by a different stride/layout and we don't rewrite per-block metadata. then idx = base + pad gets wrong mapping.

sam-sre: that matches a crash we saw in canary logs — there were `stale_kv_tag` warnings suppressed by noise filter. can you grep the service logs for "kv-tag-mismatch"? kv-bot likely logged warnings.

kv-bot: WARNING: kv-tag-mismatch detected on shard=3, page=57, expected_gen=842, found_gen=0 (suppressed 7 times)

maria-ml: exact trace from a failing run (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-06T14:02:18Z] request_id=xyZ123 start_seq=0
[2026-03-06T14:02:18Z] kv_load page=57 offset=4096 len=1024 -> tag=0
[2026-03-06T14:02:18Z] kv_store page=57 offset=4096 len=1024 -> tag=842
[2026-03-06T14:02:19Z] next_request request_id=abc987 kv_load page=57 offset=4096 len=1024 -> tag=842 (unexpected reuse) \n```

maria-ml: note the tag flips — store in one request, then a later load finds the old tag for a different request.

tim-infra: quick questions:
- do we have per-request generation id in block header?
- are we relying on zeroed pages to indicate free frames?

asha-runtime: current design relied on zero=free sentinel for speed. we also tried using a 64-bit generation counter per-block but it costs memory and increases write bandwidth.

sam-sre: short-term mitigation: invalidate page metadata at allocation (memset of header) and/or bump a global alloc-gen and compare on load. longer term: attach a compact 32-bit gen + request_id hash to each block.

maria-ml: i pushed a quick patch that zeroes headers on free; runs for 2h load test and didn't reproduce. cost: ~+5% p95 on small requests because of extra memset.

asha-runtime: important: this leak only appears when batch-shapes cause different kernel selection for consecutive requests (e.g., 1x512 then 4x128). that changes the packing so alignment assumptions break. need a test that fuzzes batch-shape transitions.

sam-sre: action items: 
- (asha) add a unit test harness that fuzzes kernel-switching + page reuse (due EOD tomorrow)
- (maria) keep the header-zeroing patch in canary for 24h and gather p50/p95 deltas
- (tim) instrument alloc path to record last_kernel_variant that used a page (so we can assert on mismatch)
- (infra) plan a rollback strategy if canary latency regression > 7%

maria-ml: also propose a quick runtime check: on kv_load, if tag==0 and page was recently used, log detailed trace (sampled 1/1000) instead of silently proceeding. that might help stability triage without perf cost.

asha-runtime: agreed. also adding a CI fuzz job that randomly mixes batch shapes across 5k iterations should catch this class of bug quickly.

tim-infra: noted. i'll create a short RFC patch with the gen-tag idea (compact 32-bit gen + 8-bit kernel-id) to discuss tradeoffs.

sam-sre: we should prioritize correctness over the small perf hit. cross-request contamination is unacceptable. schedule a short incident postmortem if we see customer hits.

maria-ml: thanks. i'll leave the canary running and post metrics in this thread. if anyone sees `kv-tag-mismatch` in prod logs, @sam-sre please ping escalation channel. :exclamation: 

kv-bot: INFO: canary run started commit=abcde1234 branch=kv-header-zeroing

maria-ml: (update 2h) canary: 0 reproductions, p95 +4.8%, p50 +0.6%. sample traces show no tag mismatches. will continue to monitor for 24h.

asha-runtime: good progress. follow-up: let's add a small benchmark that measures memset header cost with hot-path enabled on GPU to quantify exact overheads.

sam-sre: adding to backlog and will prioritize tests.

maria-ml: thanks all — filing a brief bug with repro and assigning to asha + tim.
